failure.summary: The frozen v1 graph-closure horizon and undirected LCC ladder make high-LCC worlds survive by construction, while repeated target levels can encode identical adjacency operators as multiple worlds.
proof: With an undirected graph and horizon n-1, a node reaches every node in its connected component.
If largest_weak_component_fraction L is greater than 0.5, more than half of nodes lie in that component, so median_horizon_reachable_fraction equals L.
Therefore horizon_realization_ratio = median_horizon_reachable_fraction / L equals 1 for every such world.

The frozen adequacy-complete ladder includes targets 0.75, 0.90 and approximately 0.95, so at least one high-LCC world must be predicted to survive; falsified_universe is not a reachable prediction class under this v1 construction.

In the captured NEON geometries, only 3 or 4 distinct thresholds occurred for 5 declared target levels, so identical or effectively identical structural operators were also counted multiple times in the survival fraction.
failure.consequence: The v1 forecast is not a valid three-class prospective regime test for this world-construction/horizon combination. Biological response must remain unopened.

next_protocol_requirements: Use a new protocol version rather than altering the frozen v1 protocol.

Use a finite one-transition structural horizon for both the response-blind forecast and the positive-occurrence compatibility rule, with scientific justification independent of desired forecast class balance.
Deduplicate identical structural adjacency operators before computing the falsifiable-world survival denominator.
Reuse the frozen 16-site roster and node-registry fingerprints; do not select a new candidate family in response to this method STOP.
Freeze the new rule before computing any new regime forecasts and before any biological response endpoint access.
